preamble: No documented change of a palatalized [tʲ] directly to the retroflex affricate [tʂ] was found. The Polish example formerly given here is wrong: Polish cz [tʂ] continues Proto-Slavic *č from the first palatalization of velars (*k), while Proto-Slavic *tj gave Polish c [ts] (świeca 'candle' < *světja) and *t before front vowels gave ć [tɕ] (ciało 'body'). The Polish developments of tʲ belong in t_palatalized_to_ts and in a tʲ > tɕ cell.

examples.note: *tj yields c [ts], not retroflex cz [tʂ]; Polish cz comes from velar *k (e.g. *čelo > czoło 'forehead').

sources: Stieber, Z. (1973). A Historical Phonology of the Polish Language. Carl Winter.
